To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a panel of monoclonal antibody (MAb) profiles can be used as an alternative method for typing and subtyping foot and mouth disease viruses.

(i) the use of MAb profiling in conjunction with CF and VN serological analysis provides an improved means of classifying isolates and vaccine virus strains of FMD virus; (ii) the use of this approach in conjunction with epidemiological and molecular data can provide a more accurate and comprehensive picture of FMD virus epidemiology; (iii) this information is essential for the development of effective FMD control programmes.

'The use of MAbs for antigenic profiling of SAT 2 viruses, combined with the CF test, can provide an efficient method for identifying a vaccine strain with the closest antigenic relationship to a particular isolate.'
In summary, our research is concerned with
the selection of vaccine strains of FMD virus for use in Southern Africa.
the identification of the most closely related vaccine viruses to the isolates circulating in Southern Africa.
the identification of antigenic groups of FMD viruses and the identification of vaccine viruses which are closely related to the groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vaccine strain, SAT 2/75, is the best choice of vaccine for use in southern African countries where SAT 2 viruses are prevalent.

a particular vaccine strain would be most appropriate for the control of an FMD outbreak in the area where a particular antigenic profile of the field virus was identified, and that the vaccine would provide the best possible immunogenic response to the virus.
the SAT 2 vaccine strain, O1 BFS 1860, is most closely related to the SAT 2 isolates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in Southern Africa, the SAT 2 viruses are very heterogeneous and that, in the SAT 1 and SAT 3 virus groups, the viruses are less diverse.

the MAbs have proved to be a valuable tool for the serological identification of the SAT 2 viruses, and have enabled a more detailed analysis of antigenic and serological relationships to be performed.
the MAb profiles can be used to identify antigenic relationships between FMD isolates and between isolates and vaccines.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MAb profile is a useful tool for identifying the most appropriate vaccine virus to use in a particular situation, and that it should be used in conjunction with other immunological tests to obtain a complete picture of the antigenic and immunological relationships between FMD viruses.
, in the Southern African region, a vaccine virus can be identified for each of the three SAT groups.

the use of MAb profiling in combination with serological analyses can provide a more extensive identification and classification of antigenic and serological relationships between FMD viruses, and between FMD virus strains and vaccine strains.
